title: The even-exponent Erdős–Moser equation
summary: Can a positive even power ever equal the sum of all smaller nonnegative integers raised to the same power? Ruling this out would settle the remaining case of the Erdős–Moser conjecture.

tasks.title: Restrict the base of a hypothetical solution
tasks.claim:
∀ k m : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → Even k → 2 ≤ m → powerSum k m = m ^ k →
    3 < m ∧ m % 8 = 3
tasks.role: Isolates the residue class in which an even-exponent solution could occur.
tasks.context: Use Moree's proof of Moser's theorem. Compare the sum and m^k modulo 4 to restrict m modulo 8. For an even m, grouping the sum into blocks modulo its exact power of two gives a nonzero residue, contradicting m^k. Handle m=3 separately using 1+2^k < 3^k for k≥2.

tasks.title: Exclude solutions in the remaining residue class
tasks.claim: ∀ k m : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → Even k → 3 < m → m % 8 = 3 → powerSum k m ≠ m ^ k
tasks.role: Would rule out every candidate left by Moser's restriction.
tasks.context: This is the open step. Start from the congruences for prime divisors of m−1, m+1, 2m−1 and 2m+1 in Moree. They constrain the exponent and the reciprocal sums but yield finite lower bounds. A contradiction has to cover arbitrarily large m. Record any narrower provable claim in a give-up report.
